ids: test/control_plane/production-schema.test.ts::target only > the second connection is configured the way the source configures it
target_only_tests.note: Target-only. The second connection this file opens to drive interleaved transactions is a test mechanism, and the source configures it deliberately (isolation_level=None, foreign_keys = ON, busy_timeout = 0). This test pins that configuration, so a helper that quietly stopped applying it would fail here rather than making the commit-order case pass for the wrong reason. It translates no source case and is not counted as ported coverage.

entries.reason: The source's second_connection passes isolation_level=None to switch off Python's implicit transaction management; better-sqlite3 has none to switch off, so that argument has no counterpart and the two remaining pragmas (foreign_keys = ON, busy_timeout = 0) are applied explicitly -- busy_timeout via both the constructor's timeout option and the pragma, because better-sqlite3's default is 5,000 ms. sqlite3.OperationalError(match='locked|busy') becomes expectSqliteError on the SQLITE_BUSY/SQLITE_LOCKED family AND the same message pattern (D-0016), keeping both halves. Every assertion, both writers, the reader and the interleaving are kept verbatim; the target-only case 'the second connection is configured the way the source configures it' pins the two pragmas so the helper cannot silently stop applying them.

entries.reason: The source reads PRAGMA table_info positionally as row[1] (name) and row[4] (dflt_value). better-sqlite3 exposes pragma results only as objects, so the same two columns are read by their pragma-documented names. Verified that dflt_value is null exactly when the column has no DEFAULT and a string otherwise, so the assertion is still live rather than vacuous. The table enumeration, the _at_ms/_at suffix rule and the failure message are unchanged.

inherited_limitations.topic: sqlite3.IntegrityError and OperationalError are matched as result-code families.
inherited_limitations.status: inherited from the driver, recorded under D-0016
inherited_limitations.detail: better-sqlite3 raises one error type for everything, so IntegrityError becomes /^SQLITE_CONSTRAINT/ and OperationalError becomes /^SQLITE_(BUSY|LOCKED)/. Python's IntegrityError also covers a few codes outside SQLITE_CONSTRAINT* (SQLITE_MISMATCH among them) and its OperationalError covers far more than lock contention, so the port's predicate is NARROWER than the source's class on those codes. Every refusal this file's cases actually raise falls inside the narrower set, so no case is weakened; the difference would show only for a code neither suite provokes.

inherited_limitations.topic: This file asserts against the DDL and required no implementation port.
inherited_limitations.detail: docs/production-schema.md section 11's verification table made executable. Its only module dependency is createProductionControlPlane; every property it pins is enforced by the SQL in src/control_plane/migrations/, which is carried byte-identically. One section 11 row is stale and is deliberately not reproduced as written -- the source says so, and the port carries that explanation across rather than silently translating the stale claim.

inherited_limitations.topic: Values read from SQLite are not re-narrowed to reproduce Python's int().
inherited_limitations.detail: Every numeric assertion compares a better-sqlite3 number against a literal. A hand-damaged row would compare unequal rather than raising as Python's int() does; no case here can reach that state, since every row is written through the DDL's own CHECKs.
